name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis

criteria.description: Elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and/or GGT indicating cholestasis
Positive anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA) >= 1:40 or AMA-M2 positive
Liver biopsy showing non-suppurative destructive cholangitis (florid duct lesion) and granulomatous destruction of interlobular bile ducts
PBC-specific ANA (anti-sp100, anti-gp210) in AMA-negative patients

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least 2 of 3: cholestatic biochemistry, positive AMA (or PBC-specific ANA), and compatible liver histology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis can often be made without liver biopsy if AMA is positive and cholestatic liver enzymes are present. AMA-negative PBC (~5%) may have PBC-specific ANA (anti-sp100, anti-gp210).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Florid duct lesion on liver biopsy
pathognomonic.notes: Granulomatous destruction of interlobular bile ducts; pathognomonic but not always seen

common.notes: Most common symptom; poorly correlated with disease severity
Can be severe and debilitating; often worse at night

occasional.notes: Metabolic bone disease from cholestasis-related vitamin D malabsorption

rare.notes: Indicates advanced cirrhosis; can occur before cirrhosis (nodular regenerative hyperplasia)

rare.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (A, D, E, K)

laboratory: AMA positive (>95%; anti-M2 component most specific)
Elevated total cholesterol (especially with advanced cholestasis)
Bilirubin elevated in advanced disease (prognostic marker)
PBC-specific ANA: anti-sp100 (nuclear dots), anti-gp210 (nuclear membrane)
imaging: Ultrasound: normal or hepatomegaly; excludes biliary obstruction
MRCP: normal intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts (distinguishes from PSC)
Transient elastography: liver stiffness for fibrosis staging
other: Liver biopsy: florid duct lesion (granulomatous cholangitis), portal inflammation, ductopenia, fibrosis staging (Ludwig stages I-IV or Scheuer stages)

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic bile duct changes on MRCP (beading/strictures)

redFlags: Rising bilirubin (indicates progressive disease/need for transplant evaluation)
Inadequate response to UDCA (ALP >1.67x ULN after 12 months of therapy)
Overlap features with autoimmune hepatitis (elevated ALT, high IgG)
references: Lindor KD, et al. Primary Biliary Cholangitis: 2018 Practice Guidance from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases. Hepatology. 2019;69(1):394-419.
European Association for the Study of the Liver. EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: The diagnosis and management of patients with primary biliary cholangitis. J Hepatol. 2017;67(1):145-172.
Lleo A, et al. Primary biliary cholangitis. Lancet. 2020;396(10266):1915-1926.
